raw_prompt: What is the difference between open assistant and ChatGPT? Why should i use Open Assistant? And can you give me some examples of advanced chatbots that are similar to Open Assistant?
prompt_sent: What is the difference between open assistant and ChatGPT? Why should i use Open Assistant? And can you give me some examples of advanced chatbots that are similar to Open Assistant?
response_text:
Assuming you mean **Open Assistant by LAION**, not OpenAI’s “Assistants API”: **Open Assistant was an open-source ChatGPT-like project**, while **ChatGPT is OpenAI’s proprietary hosted AI assistant**.

The short version: **ChatGPT is usually the better everyday product; Open Assistant is more interesting if you care about openness, self-hosting, research, customization, or learning how assistant models are built.** One important update: the original Open Assistant project has **concluded**, and its free public chat instance is no longer available, though its code, datasets, and model releases remain useful. LAION’s docs explicitly say “Open Assistant has now concluded,” and the FAQ says the public instance is no longer available due to the project’s conclusion. Sources: [Open Assistant docs](https://projects.laion.ai/Open-Assistant/docs/intro), [Open Assistant FAQ](https://projects.laion.ai/Open-Assistant/docs/faq).

**Open Assistant vs ChatGPT**

| Area | Open Assistant | ChatGPT |
|---|---|---|
| Creator | LAION + worldwide volunteers | OpenAI |
| Current status | Original project concluded; artifacts remain available | Actively maintained product |
| Openness | Code, data, and some model weights are available, with model licenses depending on the base model | Proprietary hosted service; model weights are not public |
| Main goal | Democratize assistant-style LLMs and make them modifiable, runnable, and researchable | Provide a polished general-purpose AI assistant for consumers, teams, and developers |
| Deployment | Can be run locally or self-hosted with enough hardware and setup | Mainly cloud-hosted via ChatGPT web/mobile/desktop and OpenAI API |
| Ease of use | More technical; not ideal as a plug-and-play daily assistant today | Easy to use, polished UI, accounts, apps, plans, support |
| Capabilities | Depends on the specific open model you run; many OA models are older | Strong general reasoning, writing, coding, image/file analysis, web search, voice/images depending on plan |
| Customization | You can inspect, modify, fine-tune, and integrate the code/models | You can customize behavior through instructions, custom GPTs, tools, and API, but not inspect or modify the core model |
| Privacy/control | Stronger if self-hosted locally, because prompts can stay on your machine | Data goes to OpenAI’s service, though ChatGPT has privacy controls such as temporary chats and data export/delete options |
| Cost | Model/data may be free, but compute can be expensive | Free and paid plans; API usage is paid separately |

OpenAI describes ChatGPT as an AI assistant for brainstorming, writing, studying, planning, math, coding, image/file analysis, and more; it is available on the web and mobile apps, can search the web, and has plan-dependent access to tools like file/image analysis. Source: [OpenAI Help Center: What is ChatGPT?](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12677804).

**Why Use Open Assistant?**

You should consider Open Assistant, or more realistically its descendants and similar open-source/local tools, if these matter to you:

1. **You want transparency.**  
   Open Assistant was designed around open code, open data, and publicly available models. That is useful for researchers, developers, students, and organizations that want to inspect how the system works instead of treating it as a black box.

2. **You want to run or modify an assistant yourself.**  
   Open Assistant’s vision was a chat assistant that could eventually run on consumer or professional hardware and integrate with third-party apps and retrieval systems. The project’s GitHub describes it as a chat assistant that can understand tasks, interact with third-party systems, and retrieve information dynamically. Source: [LAION-AI/Open-Assistant GitHub](https://github.com/LAION-AI/Open-Assistant).

3. **You care about local control and privacy.**  
   If you run an open model locally, your prompts and documents can stay on your machine. This is useful for sensitive drafts, internal documents, private notes, or offline experimentation. The tradeoff is that local models usually require technical setup and may be weaker than top hosted models.

4. **You want to fine-tune or build on top of assistant data.**  
   The OpenAssistant datasets on Hugging Face are still useful for training, evaluation, and research. The Hugging Face OpenAssistant page lists models and datasets such as `oasst1` and `oasst2`. Source: [OpenAssistant on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/OpenAssistant).

5. **You want to learn how RLHF-style assistant training works.**  
   Open Assistant was built around collecting human-written prompts, ranking responses, training reward models, and fine-tuning assistants. That makes it useful as an educational and research artifact.

6. **You want a base for experimentation, not just a polished chatbot.**  
   If your goal is “I want the best assistant for work today,” use ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, or another current hosted system. If your goal is “I want to understand, modify, host, or benchmark assistant models,” Open Assistant-style tools are more relevant.

**When You Should Not Use Open Assistant**

You probably should not choose the original Open Assistant as your main daily chatbot in 2026 if you want the strongest answers, current web features, image understanding, polished apps, enterprise admin, or reliable support. The original public instance is no longer available, and many OpenAssistant models listed on Hugging Face were last updated around 2023. For most practical use, you would use a newer open model through a modern interface instead.

**Advanced Chatbots and Tools Similar to Open Assistant**

Here are good examples, split by what “similar” means.

**Open-source or local-first alternatives**

1. **HuggingChat**  
   HuggingChat is probably the closest spiritual successor for many users: a chat app powered by open-source AI models, with a model chooser and Hugging Face ecosystem integration. Its page says it is “powered by open source AI models” and lets users choose available open models. Source: [HuggingChat](https://huggingface.co/chat/).  
   Best for: trying open models without setting up your own machine.

2. **Open WebUI**  
   Open WebUI is a self-hosted AI interface that can connect to local or cloud models, including Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, and compatible APIs. It supports conversations, tools, retrieval/search, voice/vision features, and organization controls. Source: [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/).  
   Best for: building your own private ChatGPT-like interface for local models, teams, or mixed local/cloud setups.

3. **Jan**  
   Jan is an open-source ChatGPT-style desktop app focused on personal/local AI. It lets you use open models and also connect to online models like OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, and others. Source: [Jan](https://www.jan.ai/).  
   Best for: a desktop app that feels closer to ChatGPT but gives you more local control.

4. **GPT4All**  
   GPT4All is a private local chatbot for running LLMs on everyday desktops and laptops. It supports local document chat and does not require API calls or a GPU for many setups. Sources: [GPT4All docs](https://docs.gpt4all.io/), [Nomic GPT4All](https://www.nomic.ai/gpt4all).  
   Best for: offline/private document chat on a personal computer.

5. **Ollama + Open WebUI**  
   Ollama itself is more of a local model runner than a chatbot, but paired with Open WebUI it becomes a strong local ChatGPT-like stack. You can run models like Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma, and others, depending on your hardware.  
   Best for: developers who want local models with a clean web UI.

6. **AnythingLLM**  
   AnythingLLM is a self-hostable AI workspace for chatting with documents, knowledge bases, and different LLM providers. It is not the same kind of project as Open Assistant, but it fits the same “own your assistant stack” category.  
   Best for: private RAG/document assistants for personal or team knowledge bases.

7. **LocalAI**  
   LocalAI is a self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible local AI server. It is more backend/API-oriented than chat-oriented, but it can power chatbots and agents with local models.  
   Best for: developers who want a local replacement for OpenAI-compatible APIs.

**Advanced hosted chatbot alternatives**

These are less “open” than Open Assistant, but similar in that they are advanced general-purpose assistants:

1. **Claude by Anthropic**  
   Strong for writing, analysis, long documents, coding help, and careful reasoning.  
   Best for: long-form writing, document analysis, and nuanced explanation.

2. **Google Gemini**  
   Strong integration with Google services, multimodal features, and general assistant tasks.  
   Best for: users already in Google’s ecosystem.

3. **Microsoft Copilot**  
   Integrates with Windows, Edge, Bing, and Microsoft 365 depending on plan.  
   Best for: Microsoft Office workflows and enterprise productivity.

4. **Perplexity**  
   Search-first AI assistant that emphasizes cited answers and current web research.  
   Best for: research, comparisons, and source-backed answers.

5. **Mistral Le Chat**  
   Mistral’s hosted assistant based on Mistral models.  
   Best for: users who want a European AI provider and access to Mistral’s model family.

6. **Meta AI**  
   Consumer-facing assistant integrated across Meta products and based on Meta’s Llama model family.  
   Best for: casual use inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, and related surfaces.

**Best Choice by Use Case**

| If you want… | Use… |
|---|---|
| Best general-purpose assistant with minimal setup | ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini |
| Open-source model experimentation | HuggingChat |
| Private self-hosted ChatGPT-like interface | Open WebUI + Ollama |
| Desktop local assistant | Jan or GPT4All |
| Local document chat | GPT4All, AnythingLLM, Open WebUI |
| Developer-controlled local API | LocalAI, Ollama, vLLM |
| Research into assistant training datasets | OpenAssistant datasets/models |
| Web-search-heavy answer engine | Perplexity |
| Enterprise productivity integration | ChatGPT Business/Enterprise, Claude Team/Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini for Workspace |

**My Practical Recommendation**

If you are a normal user who wants the best assistant for writing, coding, studying, planning, images, files, and current information, use **ChatGPT** or another current hosted assistant.

If you are a developer, researcher, student, privacy-focused user, or someone who wants to build your own assistant, use **Open Assistant as a learning/reference project**, but use newer tooling such as **HuggingChat**, **Open WebUI + Ollama**, **Jan**, or **GPT4All** for actual day-to-day open/local chatbot use.

So the reason to use Open Assistant is not that it is currently “better than ChatGPT.” It usually is not. The reason is that it represents the open-source path: more inspectable, more modifiable, more self-hostable, and more useful for people who want control over the assistant stack rather than only access to a polished cloud product.

Assuming you mean **Open Assistant by LAION**, not OpenAI’s “Assistants API”: **Open Assistant was an open-source ChatGPT-like project**, while **ChatGPT is OpenAI’s proprietary hosted AI assistant**.

The short version: **ChatGPT is usually the better everyday product; Open Assistant is more interesting if you care about openness, self-hosting, research, customization, or learning how assistant models are built.** One important update: the original Open Assistant project has **concluded**, and its free public chat instance is no longer available, though its code, datasets, and model releases remain useful. LAION’s docs explicitly say “Open Assistant has now concluded,” and the FAQ says the public instance is no longer available due to the project’s conclusion. Sources: [Open Assistant docs](https://projects.laion.ai/Open-Assistant/docs/intro), [Open Assistant FAQ](https://projects.laion.ai/Open-Assistant/docs/faq).

**Open Assistant vs ChatGPT**

| Area | Open Assistant | ChatGPT |
|---|---|---|
| Creator | LAION + worldwide volunteers | OpenAI |
| Current status | Original project concluded; artifacts remain available | Actively maintained product |
| Openness | Code, data, and some model weights are available, with model licenses depending on the base model | Proprietary hosted service; model weights are not public |
| Main goal | Democratize assistant-style LLMs and make them modifiable, runnable, and researchable | Provide a polished general-purpose AI assistant for consumers, teams, and developers |
| Deployment | Can be run locally or self-hosted with enough hardware and setup | Mainly cloud-hosted via ChatGPT web/mobile/desktop and OpenAI API |
| Ease of use | More technical; not ideal as a plug-and-play daily assistant today | Easy to use, polished UI, accounts, apps, plans, support |
| Capabilities | Depends on the specific open model you run; many OA models are older | Strong general reasoning, writing, coding, image/file analysis, web search, voice/images depending on plan |
| Customization | You can inspect, modify, fine-tune, and integrate the code/models | You can customize behavior through instructions, custom GPTs, tools, and API, but not inspect or modify the core model |
| Privacy/control | Stronger if self-hosted locally, because prompts can stay on your machine | Data goes to OpenAI’s service, though ChatGPT has privacy controls such as temporary chats and data export/delete options |
| Cost | Model/data may be free, but compute can be expensive | Free and paid plans; API usage is paid separately |

OpenAI describes ChatGPT as an AI assistant for brainstorming, writing, studying, planning, math, coding, image/file analysis, and more; it is available on the web and mobile apps, can search the web, and has plan-dependent access to tools like file/image analysis. Source: [OpenAI Help Center: What is ChatGPT?](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12677804).

**Why Use Open Assistant?**

You should consider Open Assistant, or more realistically its descendants and similar open-source/local tools, if these matter to you:

1. **You want transparency.**  
   Open Assistant was designed around open code, open data, and publicly available models. That is useful for researchers, developers, students, and organizations that want to inspect how the system works instead of treating it as a black box.

2. **You want to run or modify an assistant yourself.**  
   Open Assistant’s vision was a chat assistant that could eventually run on consumer or professional hardware and integrate with third-party apps and retrieval systems. The project’s GitHub describes it as a chat assistant that can understand tasks, interact with third-party systems, and retrieve information dynamically. Source: [LAION-AI/Open-Assistant GitHub](https://github.com/LAION-AI/Open-Assistant).

3. **You care about local control and privacy.**  
   If you run an open model locally, your prompts and documents can stay on your machine. This is useful for sensitive drafts, internal documents, private notes, or offline experimentation. The tradeoff is that local models usually require technical setup and may be weaker than top hosted models.

4. **You want to fine-tune or build on top of assistant data.**  
   The OpenAssistant datasets on Hugging Face are still useful for training, evaluation, and research. The Hugging Face OpenAssistant page lists models and datasets such as `oasst1` and `oasst2`. Source: [OpenAssistant on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/OpenAssistant).

5. **You want to learn how RLHF-style assistant training works.**  
   Open Assistant was built around collecting human-written prompts, ranking responses, training reward models, and fine-tuning assistants. That makes it useful as an educational and research artifact.

6. **You want a base for experimentation, not just a polished chatbot.**  
   If your goal is “I want the best assistant for work today,” use ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, or another current hosted system. If your goal is “I want to understand, modify, host, or benchmark assistant models,” Open Assistant-style tools are more relevant.

**When You Should Not Use Open Assistant**

You probably should not choose the original Open Assistant as your main daily chatbot in 2026 if you want the strongest answers, current web features, image understanding, polished apps, enterprise admin, or reliable support. The original public instance is no longer available, and many OpenAssistant models listed on Hugging Face were last updated around 2023. For most practical use, you would use a newer open model through a modern interface instead.

**Advanced Chatbots and Tools Similar to Open Assistant**

Here are good examples, split by what “similar” means.

**Open-source or local-first alternatives**

1. **HuggingChat**  
   HuggingChat is probably the closest spiritual successor for many users: a chat app powered by open-source AI models, with a model chooser and Hugging Face ecosystem integration. Its page says it is “powered by open source AI models” and lets users choose available open models. Source: [HuggingChat](https://huggingface.co/chat/).  
   Best for: trying open models without setting up your own machine.

2. **Open WebUI**  
   Open WebUI is a self-hosted AI interface that can connect to local or cloud models, including Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, and compatible APIs. It supports conversations, tools, retrieval/search, voice/vision features, and organization controls. Source: [Open WebUI](https://openwebui.com/).  
   Best for: building your own private ChatGPT-like interface for local models, teams, or mixed local/cloud setups.

3. **Jan**  
   Jan is an open-source ChatGPT-style desktop app focused on personal/local AI. It lets you use open models and also connect to online models like OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, and others. Source: [Jan](https://www.jan.ai/).  
   Best for: a desktop app that feels closer to ChatGPT but gives you more local control.

4. **GPT4All**  
   GPT4All is a private local chatbot for running LLMs on everyday desktops and laptops. It supports local document chat and does not require API calls or a GPU for many setups. Sources: [GPT4All docs](https://docs.gpt4all.io/), [Nomic GPT4All](https://www.nomic.ai/gpt4all).  
   Best for: offline/private document chat on a personal computer.

5. **Ollama + Open WebUI**  
   Ollama itself is more of a local model runner than a chatbot, but paired with Open WebUI it becomes a strong local ChatGPT-like stack. You can run models like Llama, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma, and others, depending on your hardware.  
   Best for: developers who want local models with a clean web UI.

6. **AnythingLLM**  
   AnythingLLM is a self-hostable AI workspace for chatting with documents, knowledge bases, and different LLM providers. It is not the same kind of project as Open Assistant, but it fits the same “own your assistant stack” category.  
   Best for: private RAG/document assistants for personal or team knowledge bases.

7. **LocalAI**  
   LocalAI is a self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible local AI server. It is more backend/API-oriented than chat-oriented, but it can power chatbots and agents with local models.  
   Best for: developers who want a local replacement for OpenAI-compatible APIs.

**Advanced hosted chatbot alternatives**

These are less “open” than Open Assistant, but similar in that they are advanced general-purpose assistants:

1. **Claude by Anthropic**  
   Strong for writing, analysis, long documents, coding help, and careful reasoning.  
   Best for: long-form writing, document analysis, and nuanced explanation.

2. **Google Gemini**  
   Strong integration with Google services, multimodal features, and general assistant tasks.  
   Best for: users already in Google’s ecosystem.

3. **Microsoft Copilot**  
   Integrates with Windows, Edge, Bing, and Microsoft 365 depending on plan.  
   Best for: Microsoft Office workflows and enterprise productivity.

4. **Perplexity**  
   Search-first AI assistant that emphasizes cited answers and current web research.  
   Best for: research, comparisons, and source-backed answers.

5. **Mistral Le Chat**  
   Mistral’s hosted assistant based on Mistral models.  
   Best for: users who want a European AI provider and access to Mistral’s model family.

6. **Meta AI**  
   Consumer-facing assistant integrated across Meta products and based on Meta’s Llama model family.  
   Best for: casual use inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, and related surfaces.

**Best Choice by Use Case**

| If you want… | Use… |
|---|---|
| Best general-purpose assistant with minimal setup | ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini |
| Open-source model experimentation | HuggingChat |
| Private self-hosted ChatGPT-like interface | Open WebUI + Ollama |
| Desktop local assistant | Jan or GPT4All |
| Local document chat | GPT4All, AnythingLLM, Open WebUI |
| Developer-controlled local API | LocalAI, Ollama, vLLM |
| Research into assistant training datasets | OpenAssistant datasets/models |
| Web-search-heavy answer engine | Perplexity |
| Enterprise productivity integration | ChatGPT Business/Enterprise, Claude Team/Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini for Workspace |

**My Practical Recommendation**

If you are a normal user who wants the best assistant for writing, coding, studying, planning, images, files, and current information, use **ChatGPT** or another current hosted assistant.

If you are a developer, researcher, student, privacy-focused user, or someone who wants to build your own assistant, use **Open Assistant as a learning/reference project**, but use newer tooling such as **HuggingChat**, **Open WebUI + Ollama**, **Jan**, or **GPT4All** for actual day-to-day open/local chatbot use.

So the reason to use Open Assistant is not that it is currently “better than ChatGPT.” It usually is not. The reason is that it represents the open-source path: more inspectable, more modifiable, more self-hostable, and more useful for people who want control over the assistant stack rather than only access to a polished cloud product.
